name: Great Eastern Shipping Company Ltd
title: Great Eastern Shipping Company Ltd - 500620 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Transcript is a Q4 FY21 (March 2021) earnings call, not Q2 FY27 as labelled; management gives no earnings guidance and says it is a net buyer only at its price points, with asset prices now above those levels.

capex.peers_comment: Management said shipbuilding slots and seller-side price points are constraining deals; said scrapping is low and fleet growth strong at crude tankers ~4% and product tankers ~3%.
capex.quote: So we would now not be looking at this moment at doing any further CAPEX unless of course, prices were to recorrect and come down

triggers.label: Asset prices above buy points; no capex
triggers.quote: we are really priced out of the four sectors we are in

triggers.label: Order book lowest in 25 years
triggers.quote: the order book as a percentage of the fleet for product tankers and dry bulk is at its lowest level in the last 25 -years

triggers.label: Scrapping expected to rise on regulation
triggers.quote: as night follows day, it will happen because there are lots of regulatory changes that are coming

triggers.label: Tanker demand 5-6 mb/d below pre-COVID
triggers.quote: demand continues to remain 5 to 6 million barrels a day below pre-COVID level

red_flags.label: Seafarer crew-change risk could idle vessels
red_flags.quote: some of our vessels idled because of crew changes, etc., the answer to that is yes, they could.

red_flags.label: Rig impairment and fire-damaged vessel
red_flags.quote: Greatship Rohini idling currently because she had an accident

summary.headline: GE Shipping FY21 standalone reported net profit Rs1,030 crore; normalized Rs842 crore (EPS ~Rs57), dividend Rs9/share.
summary.overview: The call covered Q4 and full-year FY21 results, which the transcript describes as a standalone reported net profit of Rs1,030 crore and normalized standalone profit of Rs842 crore. Consolidated reported profit was Rs919 crore and consolidated normalized profit Rs759 crore. Standalone NAV rose to Rs489/share from Rs454 a year earlier, while the market-value NAV range moved to Rs514-562 from Rs488-530. Management said it is not buying ships at current prices, will let it lapse and move toward net debt-free, and is positioned for volatility. The transcript is labelled Q4 FY21 in its header but the metadata period is Q2 FY27, so the period reference is inconsistent.

financial_highlights.metric: Standalone NAV per share (book, investments at cost)
Unlevered USD IRR on investments since April 2016
Standalone net debt movement, Mar 2016 to Mar 2021
financial_highlights.value: up ~$30 million, against ~$400 million net capex

segments.name: Crude and product tankers
segments.commentary: Spot earnings near operating costs (~$10,000/day cited) for the last six to eight months; Suezmax covers locked in earlier gave outperformance, with ~$14 million incremental income from Oct to Mar. Second-hand values fell ~25% for crude and 5-10% for product tankers year on year.

segments.name: Dry bulk
segments.commentary: Rates at levels not seen since 2010 across Capesize, Kamsarmax and Supramax. Two Capes and five Kamsarmaxes are spot; one Kamsarmax is fixed to Oct-2021 and one to Feb-2022. Values rose ~15-20% year on year, with ~40-50% gains in the last six months.

segments.name: LPG
segments.commentary: All LPG ships on time charter, repriced every one to two years. Two gas vessels fixed for one to two years on strong yields. Asset values up ~5-10% year on year.

segments.name: Offshore (rigs and vessels)
segments.commentary: Latest rig repriced ~40-50% higher than prior contract (~3.5 years earlier). Rig utilisation in the 60s%, vessel utilisation ~44-45%. Seven offshore vessels reprice in H1 FY22; 18 of 19 vessels were working, with Greatship Rohini idle after a fire. Rig Greatdrill Chaaya is idle with bidding pending. Jackup coverage for next year at 72%.

guidance_outlook: Management said on the call that it does not give guidance on future earnings.
Crude and product tanker demand is 5-6 million barrels/day below pre-COVID; research houses see a return to that level by end-2021, but management said this remains to be seen.

Management said it is not buying ships or rigs at current prices and will let opportunities pass; it expects to reach net debt-free if asset prices stay where they are, to build buying power for the next downturn.

Dry bulk: management said it cannot predict how long the freight rally lasts, is positioned to benefit from both short and long-term markets, and said freight could revert to a 20% long-term median of commodity prices, implying further upside.

Offshore: management said rig repricing is improving, with the next tender under process; boats are flat with no improvement expected and rigs expected to recover before boats, which need utilisation of about 60-65% for pricing power to return.

Scrapping is expected to rise within about two years from ballast water treatment retrofit costs, CY22-23 EEXI/CII norms and terminal age limits, though management said it cannot forecast beyond six years.
capex_capacity: Fleet at 46 ships, with one Supramax due within days to take it to 47. One vessel delivery's capex already funded; no new capex planned.
Management said it is not buying at current asset prices, which are above its price points, and will remain disciplined and not a momentum buyer.
Near-miss on a crude newbuilding contract and a small rig deal, both lost. Recent offshore asset repricing at ~40-50% above the previous level.
Board approved a Rs1,000 crore NCD enabling resolution (annual) but no current plan to issue; financing roughly 70% bonds and 30% ECB.
demand_pricing: Crude and product demand still 5-6 million barrels/day below pre-COVID levels; tanker fleet growth ~4% crude and ~3% product, with minimal scrapping.
Dry bulk demand broad-based (iron ore, grains, coal); port congestion at 2010-11 levels; long-haul Brazil-China freight ~$30/t, about 16% of iron ore at ~$200/t vs a 20% long-term median.
Order book as % of fleet for product tankers and dry bulk at its lowest in at least 25 years (<6% and ~7%); crude tanker orderbook lowest since 2013.
Management cited ~$70/bbl crude and possible OPEC+ (about 2 mb/d) and Iran (about 1.5 mb/d) supply additions as drivers of optimism that keeps old ships trading.
Expects scrapping to rise from ballast water treatment costs ($400-800k per ship), EEXI/CII norms from CY22-23, and terminal age limits (e.g., 20 years).

qa_highlights.question: Why raise Rs1,000 crore via NCD when the company has cash?
qa_highlights.answer: It is an annual enabling resolution; no current plans to raise NCDs since the one vessel's capex is already funded.

qa_highlights.question: Are you positioned to capture the dry bulk and Suezmax rally given past misses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Suezmaxes were covered at higher prices, yielding ~$14 million incremental income, and both Capes and five of seven Kamsarmaxes are spot to capture the rally.

qa_highlights.question: Will you buy assets at current prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said prices are well above its price points, so it is not buying and will let opportunities pass; it has 20 acquisitions, all in the money.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net interest paid and why is the reported figure high?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said treasury income is largely investment income in mutual funds (over Rs100 crore), and interest received was about Rs28 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Are there buybacks or bonus issues planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No buyback at present because of a 22% leakage; no bonus issue under consideration.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company selling older crude tankers?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, it would like to sell a couple of older tankers, but the crew change restrictions on Indian seafarers make execution difficult; the oldest tanker is 18 years old.

risks_watch: Indian seafarer crew-change restrictions could idle vessels and block asset sales or purchases; extra COVID costs ~Rs30 crore last year.
Offshore: Greatship Rohini idle after a fire (Rs19 crore provision), Greatdrill Chaaya idle pending a contract; jackup coverage at 72% for next year, below the prior two years' full employment.
Seven offshore vessels reprice in H1 FY22; boat rates still flat with Indian boat market oversupplied.
Dry bulk cyclicality: freight at ~16% of commodity cost, vs a 20% long-term median; rates depend on commodity prices and China demand.
Scrapping expectations and order-book response to strong rates, including possible newbuilding orders.
summary.management_tone: Confident on dry bulk and rig repricing but explicitly cautious on asset values, saying it is not buying at current prices. Management was candid and at times evasive on the offshore boat market and the timing of demand recovery.
key_quotes: We are really priced out of the four sectors we are in.
So it's a 20 -0 record in our favor at the moment.
We will not be a momentum buyer.

adds.what: One Supramax vessel delivery due within days, taking fleet to 47 ships (one vessel delivery capex already funded)

growth.why: Management explicitly gives no earnings guidance; growth relies on spot rate strength in tankers and dry bulk and one Supramax delivery taking fleet to 47 ships, with no new capex planned and assets priced out of buying range.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Dry bulk rates at levels not seen since 2010 with values up ~40-50% in six months, Suezmax covers added ~$14 million incremental income Oct-Mar, and seven offshore vessels reprice in H1 FY22 with rigs repriced ~40-50% higher.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Fleet at 46 ships going to 47 with one Supramax delivery within days, but management says no new capex planned and it is not buying ships at current prices.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Fleet growth is only ~4% crude and ~3% product, and the one Supramax delivery adds ~2.2% to the fleet, while Greatship Rohini is idle and utilisation is in the 60s%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is in the 60s%, below the 80%+ level that would trigger an announcement, and management says no further capex unless asset prices correct.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no earnings guidance, but says dry bulk freight could revert to a 20% long-term median implying further upside, with rates at levels not seen since 2010.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Spot tanker earnings are near operating costs (~$10,000/day) for six to eight months, and freight rally duration is unpredictable, with boat rates flat and jackup coverage at 72% next year.

rows.label: Record-low orderbook supports rate cycle
rows.why: Product tanker orderbook below 6% of fleet and dry bulk ~7%, both at least 25-year lows, while crude tanker orderbook is lowest since 2013, limiting new supply.

rows.label: Move toward net debt-free
rows.why: Management expects to reach net debt-free if asset prices stay where they are, with no buying and no new capex planned.

rows.label: Scrapping rise from EEXI/CII and ballast water norms
rows.why: Ballast water retrofit costs of $400-800k per ship, CY22-23 EEXI/CII norms and terminal age limits are expected to lift scrapping within about two years, though management cannot forecast beyond six years.

tone.note: Management was confident on dry bulk and rig repricing and disciplined on asset prices, saying it is not buying at current levels; analysts pushed on capital allocation (NCD raise, buybacks, net interest) and the offshore boat market, where management was candid and at times evasive on recovery timi
